title: Back to School
objectives: Use a glossary or dictionary to find or check what a word means
Ask a question about something I heard
Use topic words (school subjects) correctly when I speak
Slow down and pause at a comma when a text is harder
Use clues in the sentence to guess what a new word means
Answer questions using words straight from the text

vocabulary.definition: something you learn about at school, like maths or science
the subject where we learn about the world and how it works
vocabulary.example: In science, we look at plants and animals.

vocabulary.definition: the subject where we learn about people, places and the UAE
vocabulary.example: We learn about maps in social studies.

vocabulary.definition: the subject where we learn about Islam and being kind and good
Creative Computing, Design and Innovation: we make and design things with computers
vocabulary.example: Hessa likes CCDI because it is fun.

vocabulary.definition: the subject where we learn about numbers
vocabulary.example: We add and take away numbers in maths.

vocabulary.definition: the subject where we learn to read, write and speak English
vocabulary.example: We read a story in English today.

vocabulary.definition: the subject where we draw, paint and make things
vocabulary.example: I painted a picture of the sea in art.

vocabulary.definition: the one you like the most
not hard; you can do it without trouble
hard; not easy to do or understand
makes you want to know more
vocabulary.example: This book about space is interesting.

vocabulary.definition: not interesting; it makes you feel tired
vocabulary.example: Waiting in the car is boring.
Our classroom is bright and clean.

vocabulary.definition: a person who helps students learn
vocabulary.example: Our teacher reads us a story.
We learn new words every day.

sentences.text: I like science because it is interesting.
We learn about people and places in social studies.
Hessa likes CCDI because it is fun.

grammar.title: Giving reasons: because
explain: I like science because it is interesting.
Why do you like art? Because it is fun!
examples: I like CCDI because it is fun.
I like social studies because it is interesting.
I do not like maths because it is difficult.

practice.prompt: I like science ___ it is interesting.

practice.answer: I like maths because it is easy.
She likes art because it is fun.

grammar.title: Asking questions
explain: We ask questions to find out more.
What asks about a thing. Why asks for a reason. Who asks about a person.
A question ends with a question mark ?

practice.prompt: ___ do you like science? Because it is interesting.
What goes at the end of a question?

grammar.title: like / likes
explain: I like, you like, we like, they like.
With he, she or a name, add -s: he likes, Hessa likes.
Not liking: I do not like / he does not like.

practice.explain: After does not, we use like with no -s.

reading.title: The First Day Back
paragraphs: Today is the first day back at school. The classroom is bright and clean. Miss Huda smiles and says, "Welcome back, Grade 3!"
Miss Huda asks, "What is your favourite subject?" Salem puts up his hand. "My favourite subject is maths," he says. "I like maths because I like numbers. It is easy for me."
Noora likes science. "Science is interesting," she says. "We learn about plants, animals and the sky. It is difficult sometimes, but I love it."
Mariam likes CCDI best. She likes making things on the computer. Her friend Noora also likes CCDI. "It is never boring!" says Mariam.

questions.prompt: What do they learn about in science?
Which subject is difficult sometimes for Noora?

choices: it makes you want to know more
questions.answer: it makes you want to know more

items: Miss Huda asks about favourite subjects.
Mariam says CCDI is never boring.
